cycle_position.summary: Affordability-crisis beneficiary with a repricing underway: national average cap ~5.9% early 2026 (down ~40 bps from Q4 2024) even as REIT implied caps normalized hard (4.44% Q1 2025 -> 6.59% Q4 2025). Tiered market: premium 200+ lot city-utility parks 4-5%; stabilized 5-7%; value-add (below-market rents, park-owned-home cleanup, utility issues) 7-9.5%. Private equity active and consolidating.

supply_demand.value: Essentially zero new community supply (zoning hostility) against a deepening affordability crisis — the structural long.

debt_terms.value: Agency (Fannie/Freddie MHC programs) at 50+ lots with standards; small parks = local bank/seller financing.

small_investor_verdict.entry_vehicle: A 30-80 lot value-add park in a secondary/tertiary East Coast market (PA/upstate NY/Southside VA/Carolinas), tenant-owned homes preferred, at the 7-9.5% tier.
small_investor_verdict.reasoning: The value-add math rhymes with the buyer's core skill (fix infrastructure, raise below-market lot rents toward market, convert park-owned homes to tenant-owned) at yields the 2-4 unit market can't reach. Watch-outs: East Coast park inventory is scarcer than the Midwest/Southeast, PE competition is real at the quality tiers, several states are adding MHC-specific tenant protections (rent-increase notice, opportunity-to-purchase on park sales) — screen each state's MHC statute before offering; not yet in the rules engine.

gaps: MD/VA/PA/NC MHC-specific statutes (lot-rent notice, park-sale opportunity-to-purchase) — add to regulatory_rules
